title: openai-chat-completions-parity-params-roles-stop-logprobs-formatting-streaming-stability
author: Jordan Lee
release_notes: Added OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity for params, roles, stop/logprobs and response formatting; improved streaming stability and fixed function-calling edge cases. Backwards compatible with existing Redwood chat API.
description: Motivation: Customers relying on OpenAI-compatible chat completions expect parity for params, role semantics, stop sequences, logprobs, and subtle response formatting behaviors. This PR implements the OpenAI /v1/chat.completions compatibility layer updates and addresses several streaming stability regressions discovered in production canaries. What this PR does: - Add support for OpenAI-style request params (temperature, top_p, n, max_tokens, presence_penalty, frequency_penalty) mapping into Redwood's unified inference config. - Normalize role handling so assistant/system/user semantics match OpenAI edge cases (empty roles, role aliases). - Implement stop sequence processing for both text and tokenized stop sequences; ensure stop triggers stream termination consistently across batching. - Surface logprobs when requested (top_k/top_p integration and token-level scores) through the openai_compat layer while preserving Redwood's tokenization pipeline. - Improve streaming stability: fix race in stream_manager that caused partial chunks to be dropped on sudden KV cache eviction; add backpressure and retry hooks for transient transport errors. - Response formatting: ensure content concatenation, function call structures, and choice indices match OpenAI behavior for multi-choice responses. Checklist: [x] unit tests added/updated [x] integration tests for streaming and function-calls [x] docs updated (openai_compat) [x] performance regression tested on perf-canary [x] feature gated behind compat flag. Compatibility notes: The compat layer is feature-flagged (OPENAI_COMPAT=on) and defaults to Redwood's prior behavior when off. Existing Redwood SDKs are unaffected unless users opt into the OpenAI compatibility endpoint. We added thorough diffs in integration tests to assert token boundaries and logprob values. Summary of impact: Enables smoother migrations for customers using OpenAI-style APIs, eliminates several production streaming flakiness cases, and exposes logprob outputs required by some evaluation pipelines. No breaking API changes expected.
commits: feat(openai-compat): implement core /v1/chat.completions param mapping and role normalization
fix(streaming): resolve race in stream_manager causing dropped chunks during kv cache eviction
feat(openai-compat): add stop sequence handling and token-level stop detection
feat(openai-compat): surface logprobs through compat layer with opt-in flag
test(integration): add parity tests for multi-choice, function-calls, streaming termination
review_comments: Samir Gupta: Overall looks good; two main asks: (1) add a defensive timeout around KV cache eviction to avoid long blocking in stream path, (2) add an integration test for stop sequences that include unicode/emoji separators.
Jordan Lee: Addressed both in follow-up commits. Introduced eviction grace window with a configurable flag and added test coverage for multi-byte stop tokens.
Priya Nair: Noted a potential perf regression in the high-concurrency canary (>500 qps). Can you run the canary and include resultados?
Jordan Lee: Ran perf-canary with new config; no >5% p95 latency regression observed. Results uploaded to perf-canary artifact link in Linear ENG-1042.
Diego Morales: Left a small nits on naming (response_formatter -> response_serializer) but approves the changes; suggested follow-up cleanup.
Samir Gupta: Approved after the eviction grace window and additional tests. CI green on rerun.
